items.title: 4 New SUVs To Be Unveiled In December: Honda Avencier To Next-Generation Toyota Fortuner
points: The month of December this year is going to be an important month for SUV lovers.
First off, we have the new-generation Toyota Fortuner, which will be making its global debut on December 1, 2026.
As for its official India launch, it is expected to take place in early 2027.
Coming to the design, the new-generation Fortuner is expected to get a larger grille, slimmer LED headlamps, redesigned bumpers and muscular wheel arches.
And on the inside, Toyota could offer a 12.3-inch touchscreen, digital instrument cluster, panoramic sunroof, ventilated seats and Level 2 ADAS.
This motor currently produces around 201 PS and up to 500 Nm of torque in India.
Apart from this, there are reports of a possible petrol strong-hybrid version based on Toyota's 2.7-litre engine.
In addition to the Toyota Fortuner new-generation model, Honda is also getting ready to unveil its new Avancier on December 1.

items.title: NVIDIA stock crash: Why did AMD, Broadcom shares rise up to 5% after Jensen Huang's exit? Experts' views
points: NVIDIA stock crash: Shares of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Broadcom rallied on Thursday, November 12, even as NVIDIA shares tumbled following the sudden resignation of its co-founder and long-serving CEO, Jensen Huang.

AMD shares climbed around 5.86%, while Broadcom advanced 5.54% during Thursday's trading session, as investors assessed whether Nvidia's leadership turmoil could create fresh opportunities for competing semiconductor companies.
Nvidia shares, meanwhile, fell as much as 4.34% during the Thursday's session.

According to market experts, the dramatic development has sent shockwaves through the global artificial intelligence (AI) industry, given Huang's instrumental role in transforming Nvidia into the world's leading supplier of graphics processing units (GPUs)…
The company's Chief Financial Officer (CFO), Colette Kress, has been appointed interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.
The leadership change comes amid reports concerning Huang's personal relationships and questions around corporate governance and potential national security implications.

items.title: Mind the gap: Partial opening of Namma Metro Pink Line leaves commuters wanting
points: A view of the Namma Metro Pink Line in Bengaluru. | Photo Credit: SUDHAKARA JAIN “Every day, I travel on this route by bus.

There is no point in taking the metro if I still have to depend on a bus to reach my destination,” says Shankar Prasad, an office-goer from Hulimavu in south Bengaluru.
For Shankar, who travels every day to the Central Business District (CBD), the partial opening of Namma Metro’s Pink Line only means another long wait.

items.title: Sriperumbudur toll plaza gets MLFF
points: Motorists using the Sriperumbudur toll plaza on the Chennai-Bengaluru National Highway from Wednesday midnight will be able to drive freely without stopping for boom barriers. .
This is the second plaza in the State to get multi-lane free flow tolling, where gantries with scanners have been installed.
The scanners will read FASTag cards and number plates, and the system will automatically collect the amount due at the toll.
The facility will allow motorists to drive through, without having to wait at the plaza, which caters to over 1.25 lakh vehicles on a daily basis.

items.title: Choosing faith over fear
points: Her family had donated a significant amount of land and the freshly painted white building of William Cary Memorial Church was ready to welcome devotees at Narayantala village in Basanti block of West Bengal’s South 24 Parganas district.
Now, she shudders when she thinks about what happened on that Saturday afternoon to the church.
“The gate of the church was opened for the first and the last time on October 31.

During the inaugural function, a group entered the premises and attacked the priests and others who were participating in the ceremony,” Purnima says, recalling the attack that left her and several others injured.
She says she was hit with a stick and had to be hospitalised for a day.
After the attack, the church has been closed, but Purnima says she often goes to its door to peek at the picture of Jesus Christ through a broken window.

items.title: Chhattisgarh liquor case key accused held in UAE
points: Vikas Agrawal, a key accused in an alleged ₹2,883-crore Chhattisgarh liquor scam who was absconding for the past several years, has been caught in Dubai and may be brought to India very soon, at least three officials told HT.

The alleged irregularities pertain to the illegal sale of unaccounted and duty-evaded liquor through state-run liquor outlets, allegedly under the protection of senior excise and other Chhattisgarh government officials between 2019 and 2023.

A liquor syndicate led by businessman Anwar Dhebar and retired IAS officer Anil Tuteja manipulated the state’s excise system to generate illegal proceeds exceeding ₹2,883 crore, according to the Enforcement Directorate (ED).

In a statement issued on June 1 this year, while attaching assets worth ₹1,000 crore in the case, ED said that “Vikas Agrawal functioned as the ground-level financial manager of the syndicate, collecting commissions from distilleries and FL-10A (foreign…
So far, 85 people have been named as accused under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) in six charge sheets.

items.title: Inflation tops RBI’s 6% ceiling, raises December rate hike prospects
points: India’s retail inflation rose to a two-year high of 6.09% in October, breaching the Reserve Bank of India’s upper tolerance limit of 6% and strengthening expectations of another rate hike in December.
Headline inflation has risen every month since November 2025 and had crossed the RBI’s actual target of 4% in June this year.
India’s benchmark inflation rate, measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI), rose 6.1% in October, according to data released by the National Statistics Office (NSO).

Core inflation – the non-food, non-fuel component of the CPI basket, which is considered less susceptible to seasonal fluctuations – stood at 4.6%, according to data from the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE).
The RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) noted the rising trend in core inflation in its October resolution and projected it at 4.4% for the full financial year.

The chipmaker has agreed to buy about $10 billion worth of shares in Anthropic as part of a $26 billion private placement concurrent with its IPO, the AI model firm’s filings show.

Anthropic is looking to bolster demand for the IPO with a campaign of events for prospective investors, including a live-streamed event with its Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei and JPMorgan Chase & Co. CEO Jamie Dimon on Friday, a person familiar with…
The company is targeting a fully diluted valuation of about $1.4 trillion, below where some investors expected the company to settle, Bloomberg News reported.
The company reported a revenue run rate of $81 billion as of Oct.
31, up $10 billion from the end of September, the filing showed.
Anthropic had a $65 billion run rate figure at the end of July, Bloomberg News reported.

items.title: 2 missing SPOs found shot dead in Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar
points: The incident follows an attack on a CRPF checkpost in south Kashmir’s Kulgam district on Wednesday, in which three security personnel were injured, one of them critically.
“The bodies were recovered between 8am and 9am on Thursday,” a security official said, requesting anonymity.

“A massive operation is underway to identify, track and neutralise the assailants.” The deceased have been identified as Babi Chand (57) and Rashpal Kumar (45), both residents of Kiyar village in the remote Dachhan tehsil in Kishtwar.

Posted with the special operations group (SOG) of local police at Kiyar, the two were heading towards a temporary base of army’s 17 Rashtriya Rifles in the Dharna-Marwah belt on Wednesday afternoon when they went out of contact, officials said.
The slain personnel’s service weapons — an INSAS rifle and a .303 rifle along with some magazines and ammunition — were missing and are believed to have been taken away by terrorists, officials said.
Kishtwar legislator and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Shagun Parihar condemned the attack.

points: The two sides will hold the sixth round of negotiations for the trade deal this week, and economic ties and cooperation in key areas such as critical minerals and energy have been spurred by a turnaround in the overall relationship since Mark Carney was…
The two countries are looking to finalise talks on the trade deal before Prime Minister Narendra Modi visits Canada during December 11-12.

Mobility of professionals and students has emerged as a focus area for India in recent years, and migration and mobility partnerships have been concluded with close to 30 countries, most of them in Europe.
India and Canada also held their maiden migration and mobility dialogue in New Delhi on October 26.
Canada currently hosts one of the largest Indian diaspora communities, with more than 1.8 million Canadians of Indian origin and an estimated one million non-resident Indians.
India’s imports of pulses in the first quarter of 2026 were worth about $6.51 billion, with Canada accounting for $1.01 billion or 15.56% of the total.

items.title: Sukhbir Badal likely to meet Amit Shah on November 13, SAD-BJP alliance may be announced this month
points: Published - November 13, 2026 04:58 am IST - NEW DELHI/CHANDIGARH Shiromani Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal.
SAD sources said that Mr. Badal is expected to leave for New Delhi in the second half of the day, after his rally at Raikot, to meet Mr. Shah.
It is expected that the talks surrounding the seat sharing and finalisation of the alliance for the Punjab election would be on the agenda.
Even as leaders from both parties remained tight-lipped about the deliberations, the sources indicated that the announcement about the alliance could be made within November.
In August this year, Mr. Badal had met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, where the possibility of renewing the alliance was discussed.

items.title: Punjab Assembly polls: AAP releases second list of candidates
points: The ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Thursday (November 12, 2026) released its second list of thirty one candidates in Punjab for the upcoming Assembly election, due in early 2027.
Two sitting AAP Lok Sabha MPs will enter the fray: Raj Kumar Chabbewal from Phagwara and Gurmeet Singh Meet Hayer from Barnala.

The names were finalised after detailed deliberations with all members at a marathon meeting of the party’s Political Affairs Committee (PAC), chaired by AAP National Convenor Arvind Kejriwal, said a party statement.
The AAP has replaced Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khudian with his nephew Randhir Singh Dhira in Lambi.
The party has made Karamjit Singh Rintu as its candidate from Amritsar North, following its sitting MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap’s recent resignation.
On October 31, AAP released its first list of 40 candidates, all of them sitting legislators.
There are 117 Assembly seats in Punjab and the five-year term of the Assembly ends on March 16, 2027.

items.title: GPU Financing Filters Further Into ABS With Planned Newton Deal
points: (Bloomberg) -- Newton Commercial Finance, a joint venture between Apple Bank and Eagle Point Credit Management, is in early talks with investors about a potential $180 million bond offering partly backed by artificial intelligence chip loans.

Loans tied to AI chips, including graphic processing units or GPUs, make up about 15% of the collateral pool, the people said, asking not to be identified because they’re not authorized to speak publicly.
A representative for Newton Commercial Finance declined to comment.
The ABS deal would be the latest in a series of equipment loan and lease ABS that include exposure to chips.
Other ABS equipment loan and lease deals in recent months from Stonebriar Commercial Finance and Wingspire Equipment Finance also included GPU exposure.

Stonebriar last month sold an $869 million ABS offering with GPU loans accounting for roughly 15% of the collateral, while GPU loans made up about 20% of the collateral in Wingspire’s more than $407 million transaction in September.

items.title: Yen Falls to Cusp of 160 Level, Fanning Intervention Risk
points: (Bloomberg) -- The yen slid to the verge of 160 to the dollar, a key threshold that’s raising the specter that policymakers in Tokyo will swoop in again to defend the currency.
As rising US bond yields pushed the dollar higher, the yen slipped 0.1% to 159.94.

Japan’s chief currency official Atsushi Mimura on Thursday said he has a strong impression that the currency moves over the past few days have been “too fast” and reminded investors of the currency-market intervention a few months ago, when the yen hit a…

“Mimura seems to be sending a signal that 160 is some sort of line in the sand, which is always risky since markets never met a line in the sand that they didn’t want to test,” said Win Thin, chief economist at Bank of Nassau 1982.
The currency weakness reflects the significant gap in interest rates between the US and Japan, with the Bank of Japan’s benchmark set at 1.25%, more than 2.5 percentage points below the Fed’s.

items.title: LR2s Turn Dirty: A larger fleet, but fewer LR2s trading clean
points: Dirty Employment Gains Ground The LR2 market has undergone a marked change in vessel employment since the start of 2025.
Signal Ocean data show that dirty employment accounted for 74.2% of the LR2 fleet on 30 October 2026, compared with 53.0% on 1 January 2025.
Dirty-employed LR2s rose from 256 to 402 vessels, an increase of 57%, while clean-employed tonnage fell from 227 to 140, a reduction of 38%.
Clean-employed vessels outnumbered dirty units between 20 July and 17 October 2025, with the dirty share falling to 47.1% on 22 August.
Since 23 July, the share has remained above 70%, suggesting a more persistent redistribution of LR2 capacity towards dirty trades rather than a short-lived change in employment patterns.
Deployment: Relet and Spot Drive the Dirty Build The breakdown by employment type provides further insight into the redistribution of LR2 capacity.
LR2 Employment Shifts Accelerate in 2026 Weekly LR2 employment figures show a sustained reduction in clean-employed tonnage since October 2025, with the decline accelerating during 2026.

items.title: Baltic Dry Index Advances for 7th Day
points: The Baltic Exchange’s dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, was up for a seventh straight session on Thursday, rising by 2.1% to its highest since October 5 at 3,020 points.
Gains were broad-based across vessel segments, particularly the larger one.
The capesize index, which typically transports 150,000-ton cargoes, including iron ore and coal, advanced by 2.9% to its highest since October 2 at 4,836 points.

At the same time, the supramax index increased by 1.2% to an over one-week high of 1,831 points; and the panamax index, which usually carries 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, went up 0.7% to its highest level since October 22 at 2,117 points.

items.title: Dry bulk ship recycling falls 36% to 18-year low
points: Dry bulk ship recycling has been at a low level since 2021 due to strong freight rates.

These include high congestion in 2021, longer sailing distances due to sanctions on Russian coal, which caused ships to be rerouted away from the Red Sea, and growing shipments from the Atlantic to Asia.
That is equivalent to 6% of the current fleet capacity.

As ships remain in service for longer, the dry bulk fleet has gradually aged, with the average bulk carrier now over 13 years old, compared with an average of 10 years at the start of the decade,” says Gouveia.
There are now 1,035 dry bulk ships, totalling 46.7m DWT, which are more than 25 years old.
By contrast, only 11 capesize ships are more than 25 years old, since capesizes typically have shorter lifecycles.
Ship deliveries are expected to accelerate, growing 19% in 2027 and a further 4% in 2028.

items.title: Remembering the role of our ports
points: Yesterday, on Remembrance Day, we remember all those who served, those who made the ultimate sacrifice, and the families and communities whose lives were changed by conflict.
Throughout both World Wars, ports across ABP’s network played an important role in supporting Britain’s wartime efforts.
During the First World War, Southampton’s docks were requisitioned as Britain’s No. 1 Military Embarkation Port, becoming a major departure point for troops heading overseas.

Southampton became a major embarkation point for the Allied invasion of Europe, with more than 3.5 million troops and over 250,000 vehicles embarking from the port between D-Day and the end of the war.

items.title: IMO Secretary-General calls on States to enforce maritime rules in the Strait of Hormuz
points: The Secretary-General of the International Maritime Organization (IMO) Mr. Arsenio Dominguez has called for stronger action from IMO Member States to enforce maritime safety and security regulations in and around the Strait of Hormuz.

Amid continued attacks against commercial ships in the area, Secretary-General Dominguez stated: “IMO’s technical and operational regulations are there to protect seafarers, ships and the marine environment.
They must be respected and enforced effectively.

“I call on all flag States, port States and relevant coastal States to exercise their responsibilities under IMO conventions and take measures to address violations, within their respective jurisdictions, and in accordance with international law.
I strongly urge shipowners and operators to refrain from commercial activities in the Strait that expose seafarers to unacceptable risks.
It is imperative for Governments to tackle the root causes of this conflict, which has also increased the cost of living for millions of people worldwide,” he stated.

items.title: Korean partnership’s carbon capture proposal selected as basis for IMO’s future safety guidelines

The proposal builds on Korea’s multi-year OCCS development work, including raising safety concerns about the location of onboard CO₂ storage tanks in 2023 and proposing initial safety guidelines in 2024.

items.title: Hapag-Lloyd with a strong third quarter
points: Hapag-Lloyd concluded the third quarter of 2026 with a significantly higher Group EBITDA of USD 1.7 billion (EUR 1.5 billion) compared to the same period of the previous year.
Group EBIT climbed to USD 1.1 billion (EUR 0.9 billion) and Group profit to USD 1.0 billion (EUR 0.9 billion).

The main drivers for this positive development were significantly higher freight rates, strong vessel utilization in the Liner Shipping business and dynamic growth in the Terminal & Infrastructure segment.

In the Liner Shipping segment, revenue increased to USD 6.7 billion (EUR 5.8 billion) in the third quarter of 2026, driven by a significantly higher average freight rate of USD 1,808 per TEU (Q3 2025: USD 1,413 per TEU).

Transport volumes reached 3.4 million TEU, remaining in line with the prior-year quarter despite the conflict in the Middle East and weather-related operational disruptions, both of which also put pressure on unit costs.

It weighs close to 140 tonnes and will be able to store up to 200 tonnes of LBG once the facility is operational.

items.title: World’s first ammonia dual-fuel gas carrier enters service
points: The delivery of MGC ANTWERPEN has successfully completed its maiden commercial voyage, from China to India, in July 2026.
It is the world’s first ocean-going ammonia dual-fuel Medium Gas Carrier (MGC), built by HD Hyundai Heavy Industries (HD HHI) for EXMAR.
This maiden voyage means ammonia as a fuel has now entered real-world commercial service, with the potential for up to 90% fewer emissions compared with conventional fuels.

From concept to commercial operation The successful voyage is the result of several years of collaboration between EXMAR, HD Hyundai Heavy Industries (HD HHI), LR, WinGD, and Nord Gas Solutions (formerly Wärtsilä Gas Solutions).
The 46,000 m³ vessel can transport either ammonia or LPG and operates on ammonia fuel, for near-zero emission operations.

Operational experience from the first and second vessels will be incorporated into operations for the remaining ships, strengthening the design integrity, safety and reliability of the ammonia dual-fuel system.

items.title: Wallenius SOL changes name to Wallenius Link
points: Following the previously announced change in ownership, shipping company Wallenius SOL is now taking the next natural step.
From 12 November 2026 the company will operate under the name Wallenius Link.
In April 2026, Wallenius Lines entered into an agreement to acquire SOL Group’s shares in Wallenius SOL, thereby becoming the sole owner of the company.
The new ownership structure provides long-term stability and continuity, while creating a clear foundation for the company’s continued development.
“The new name, Wallenius Link, reflects something at the heart of our business and the role we play.
And behind all that are the links that enable goods to move and businesses to grow,” says Erik Nøklebye, Chairman of Wallenius Link.
Wallenius Link will remain under the leadership of the same management team and organization.
Creating the links that support critical industrial infrastructure in Northern Europe is part of our legacy, and it will remain central to our future,” says Elvir Dzanic, CEO, Wallenius Link.

items.title: Automation and portfolio adjustment impact HHLA’s results for the first nine months of the year
points: In the first nine months of 2026, the business performance of Hamburger Hafen und Logistik AG (HHLA) was still characterised by challenging conditions and operational disruptions.
In particular, the ramp-up phase for the further automation of the Hamburg container terminals and strike-related disruptions adversely affected container throughput development in the third quarter.

Group container throughput decreased by 7.3 percent to 4,446 thousand standard containers (TEU) (previous year: 4,798 thousand TEU), while container transport volumes increased by 0.5 percent to 1,509 thousand TEU (previous year: 1,501 thousand TEU).
Group revenue rose by 3.3 percent to € 1,375.1 million (previous year: € 1,331.4 million).
The operating result (EBIT) fell by 30.7 percent to € 81.2 million (previous year: € 117.1 million).

In the Container segment, container throughput at HHLA’s container terminals fell significantly in the first nine months of 2026 by 7.3 percent to 4,446 thousand standard containers (TEU) (previous year: 4,798 thousand TEU).

items.title: Japex seeks no more alternative LNG cargoes for October-March, raises JKM forecast
points: Japan Petroleum Exploration Co. Ltd. is no longer seeking alternative spot LNG cargoes for the October-March period amid the suspension of term supply from the Middle East, as the company raised its JKM price forecast for the period, Yutaka Nishimura,…
Japex has already secured two spot LNG cargoes for the April-September period and another LNG cargo for the October-March period.
The three replacement cargoes for Middle Eastern supplies will be the last for this fiscal year,” Nishimura told an earnings press conference in Tokyo.
Japex has raised its JKM price forecast to $25/MMBtu for the October-December quarter and $20/MMBtu for January-March, up from $12/MMBtu earlier for the period, Nishimura added.

In Iraq, the Gharraf oil field resumed production in late June, and it is producing in the “upper 100,000” barrels/day range, but it has not been able to ship any crude cargoes to date, Nishimura said.
Japex has not factored in revenue from crude oil sales in its earnings forecast for the fiscal year to March 2027, Nishimura said.

items.title: Bomb threat emails target BMC, Pune civic body, PNB branches; searches find nothing suspicious
points: Bomb threat emails targeting civic offices in Mumbai and Pune, along with Punjab National Bank (PNB) branches in Mumbai, triggered security checks on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
Police and bomb squad personnel searched the premises but found nothing suspicious.

According to police, threat emails were received at a Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) office and PNB branches in Zaveri Bazar and Marine Lines, claiming that explosives had been planted on the premises.
“A hoax bomb threat email was received at the BMC office and PNB Bank this morning.
Further legal process is ongoing,” Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone 2) Raghasudha R. said.
The Mumbai Mayor’s office also received a bomb threat via email, prompting police and bomb squad personnel to reach the premises and initiate an investigation.
According to sources, the email contained references to Khalistan and inflammatory remarks about the 1984 anti-Sikh violence.
Meanwhile, the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) received a bomb threat on its official email address on Thursday.

items.title: TNPDCL seeks nod to procure 3,000 MW
points: A senior TNPDCL official said amid a power demand of about 19,000 MW and an extended summer, it has been proposed to buy 3,000 MW of round-the-clock (RTC) power for five years, under the Finance, Operate and Own guidelines.

File image for representation only | Photo Credit: The Hindu The Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited (TNPDCL) has increased the quantum of its proposed power procurement from 1,500 megawatt (MW) to 3,000 MW through a medium-term tender agreement.
The TNPDCL, which submitted the proposal to procure 1,500 MW to the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission (TNERC) in February this year, has now doubled the quantum.

A senior TNPDCL official said amid a power demand of about 19,000 MW and an extended summer, it has been proposed to buy 3,000 MW of round-the-clock (RTC) power for five years, under the Finance, Operate and Own guidelines.

items.title: SS United States Sits Upright on Gulf Seafloor After Historic Sinking
points: Image courtesy SS United States: An Operational Guide to America's Flagship The SS United States has settled upright on the floor of the Gulf of Mexico, completing its transformation from record-breaking ocean liner to the world’s largest artificial reef.

Early sonar and remotely operated vehicle inspections confirmed that the 990-foot vessel came to rest upright, just feet from its intended location, following its controlled sinking off Florida’s Gulf Coast on Wednesday, November 11.
RV Explorer, a shipwreck research and salvage vessel based in Cape May, New Jersey, shared an image of diver Captain Will Hinton positioned in front of the ship’s stern.
“Happy to report the SS United States is sitting perfectly upright,” RV Explorer said.

According to Destin-Fort Walton Beach tourism officials, the ship now rests approximately 22 nautical miles offshore in about 180 feet of water, with its uppermost deck roughly 60 feet below the surface.

items.title: The morphing menace
points: The atmosphere on the campus was volatile, and the tension palpable.
Anger was writ large on the faces of students at a prominent college in central Keralam as they staged a sit-in protest outside the administrative office.
The slogans echoed the students’ agony and outrage.
The situation started slipping out of control as the agitated students threatened to take the law into their own hands.
The college authorities had to seek the help of the police to manage the situation, as the student unrest showed early signs of turning violent.
The agitation, feared the college authorities, may evolve into a law-and-order situation.
